title: Same Injection. Different Defenses. Different Risk.

data.kicker: LLM security cheat sheet · 6 injection defenses
title: Same Injection.
Different Defenses.
Different Risk.

intro.before: Prompt injection hides instructions inside text your model reads: a web page, an email, a PDF. Each defense limits
intro.highlight: what an attacker can still reach
intro.after: , and none of them is enough alone.

items.title: Injection Classifier
items.tagline: Detect attacks on the way in

bullets.text: A small model (e.g. Llama Prompt Guard) scores each text for injection attempts
Runs on user input and on retrieved pages, emails and tool results
Cheap and fast; blocks blunt attacks like “Ignore previous instructions”
Paraphrased, translated or encoded attacks can slip under the threshold
Marks untrusted text with delimiters, datamarks (^ between words) or encoding
The system prompt says marked text is data, never instructions
Nearly free: prompt changes only, with no extra model calls
Cuts attack success a lot but not to zero; a strong attack can still win
Checks output before it’s shown or run: schema, links and secrets
Blocks exfiltration through markdown images or links to unknown domains
Catches damage even when an injection got past the input checks
Only catches patterns it knows; it can’t judge every harmful action

items.title: Least-Privilege Tools
items.tagline: Give the agent only what it needs

bullets.text: Each task gets only the tools and OAuth scopes it needs, read-only by default
An injected “forward all mail” fails if send_email was never granted
Limits the blast radius of any hijack that does succeed
Needs design per workflow; scopes that are too tight break real tasks
A privileged LLM plans and calls tools but never reads untrusted text
A quarantined LLM with no tools reads the email or web page
Results come back as variables ($VAR1), never as instructions to follow
More calls and engineering; some tasks need data the planner can’t see
Pauses before sending, paying, deleting or anything irreversible
Shows the exact action and data, e.g. “Send email to X with file Y”
A strong last line of defense when every automated check misses
Too many prompts cause approval fatigue; gate only the risky actions

principles.sub: Detectors get bypassed; combine detection, isolation, limits and approval.
Web pages, emails, PDFs and tool results can all carry hidden instructions.
Design so a hijacked agent can't reach secrets or irreversible actions.

rows.q: RAG over web pages or emails
Output shown as links or markdown
Agent that can send or delete

quote.big: Assume the model will be fooled. Plan for it.
quote.small: Defense in depth beats any single filter.
